What is an eye donation?
Who is eligible to donate eyes?
What are cornea and corneal transplantation?
What is an eye bank, and how do you make contact for eye donation?
What precautions are to be taken by relatives?
What is the procedure of eye collection?
What are the possible complications or disfigurements during eye collection?
What happens after eye donation?
How do I ensure that the eyes donated will be used rightly?

Eye donation refers to pledging to donate one\'s eyes after death. Donated eyes are used for corneal blind patients to restore vision. It is a voluntary act done for the benefit of society, which causes no harm to the sentiments and religious faiths of the deceased family. In most circumstances, one persons eyes can help rebuild the vision of two blinds.

• Eyes can be donated by anyone, irrespective of age, sex, or blood group.
• Eyes affected by eye problems of short-sightedness, long-sightedness, astigmatism, or even operated cataract surgery are still eligible for an eye donation since the cornea is not affected by these eye problems.
• Health diseases: diabetics, hypertension, and asthma, which are not communicable, still allow one to donate their eyes.
• Diseases that make one ineligible to donate eyes are AIDS, Hepatitis B or C, rabies, septicemia, acute leukemia, tetanus, cholera, meningitis, or encephalitis.
• Eyes unfit medically for the donation are utilized for medical research and studies.

The cornea is the front transparent layer of the eyes. It is significant for the vision and its focus. If the cornea becomes cloudy for any reason, it results in vision loss, also known as corneal blindness. Corneal transplantation is a surgery that includes the replacement of the defective cornea with a healthy cornea received by eye donation.

An eye bank is a charitable organization that preserves, collects, examines, and provides donated eyes. It is formed and administered under strict medical standards. India\'s eye bank helpline number is 1919, toll-free and available 24×7. It helps regarding eye donation as well as related information.

• The eyes of the deceased are to be closed, or moist cotton can be placed over the eyes.
• Raise the donor's head about six inches to reduce the bleeding during eye collection with a pillow.
• Switch off all the fans.
• Cover the deceased's forehead with an ice pack or polythene filled with ice cubes.
• To prevent eye infections, instill antibiotic eye drops at regular intervals.
• Notify the eye bank as soon as possible.

After informing the eye bank about the donation, a team of an eye doctor, a grief counselor, and trained staff is sent to the deceased\'s place or hospital. The team will take the written consent of the family before processing further. Also, questions about medical history are asked. With great efficiency and under strict aseptic standards, eyes are collected in privacy, taking not more than ten minutes. The defective area over the eyes is restored carefully.

There is temporary bleeding caused in the area from where eyes are collected, in case the whole eyeball is obtained. The medical team works with high precision; eyes are properly closed to save any disfigurement. There is another method where only the cornea is collected instead of the whole eyeball, which is later replaced by a plastic cornea to cause no disfigurement.

• Eye bank acknowledges the donor's family with a certificate of appreciation.
• The medical team takes the collected eyes to the eye bank for examination.
• The examination includes different tests by the corneal surgeon on the tissue.
• As per the waiting list, the recipient of the eyes is contacted for a corneal transplant.
• A corneal transplant is done, which is followed by a regular examination.

Eye donation is a legal act. All eye banks are registered and operated under the Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994. The government takes strict actions in case of any complaint against the eye bank.

In India, visual impairment is a significant public health concern, affecting many of the population. Many individuals lose sight due to corneal diseases or injuries, leading to a diminished quality of life. However, there is hope; eye donation is a powerful and compassionate gesture that can restore sight to those in need. Unfortunately, there is also a huge demand-supply gap for eye donation in India due to a lack of awareness about cadaveric transplantation, the eye donation process, and the availability of eye banks.

 "DEEP " mobile application is your gateway to understanding and participating in the noble act of eye donation. This app is designed to inform, inspire, and facilitate eye donation in India, where millions of people suffer from visual impairments, often preventable or treatable through corneal transplantation.

 Our mobile app is your comprehensive resource for everything related to eye donation in India, from understanding the importance of eye donation to finding donation centres (eye banks) and even becoming an eye donor.

 Let's embark on a journey to make a meaningful impact on the lives of those struggling with vision loss.
